newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays soft vs dollar in range trading.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays soft vs dollar in range trading.

text.p: The ringgit was trapped in a tight range after a lacklustre trading session due to lack of fresh leads, dealers said.
They said offshore ringgit selling pressured the Malaysian unit but its fall was cushioned by commercial demand.
"Trading was very quiet throughout and I don't see much movement in London or New York either," said a dealer with a European bank in Kuala Lumpur.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5148/58 a dollar against 2.5117/27 at the close of Kuala Lumpur on Friday.
Dealers said muted dollar/majors movements also limited activity in the dollar/ringgit.

They said the ringgit could come under fresh selling pressure from offshore players, but immediate upside for the dollar/ringgit was likely to be capped at 2.5200 due to fears of intervention by Bank Negara.
The central bank was rumoured to be checking rates at 2.5190/5200 on Wednesday.
"Unless there's a change in fundamentals, we should see a lot of dollar selling at between 2.5180 and 2.5200," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
